userStories.title: Up recalls the queued messages into the prompt
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let up on an empty chat prompt move all queued messages into an editable multiline draft and advertise the key in the footer and /help.

**Motivation** — A user who notices a typo, or changes their mind while the agent works, has no way to correct the follow-up before it goes.

**Approach** — Integration

Read-only symbols (verified on `main` at `61fd429af`):

- `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/message-queue.ts`:
  - `type MessageQueue = readonly string[]`, oldest first.
  - `queueToPrompt(queue: MessageQueue, draft: string): string` joins the queued texts and the draft with `\n`, dropping empty strings.
- `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx`:
  - `queueRef: React.MutableRefObject<MessageQueue>` is the queue ahead of React; the drain reads it after `await`s.
  - `replaceQueue(next: MessageQueue): void` writes `queueRef.current` and `setQueued` together.
  - `EMPTY_QUEUE` is the empty queue constant.
  - `queueReturn(text: string): boolean` is passed to `ChatInput` as `onQueue`: an owner callback the input runs inside its key handler, the precedent the new callback follows.
  - `drainQueue(outcome)` already restores the queue into the prompt on a non-completed turn with `replaceQueue(EMPTY_QUEUE)` then `restorePrompt(queueToPrompt(queue, editorRef.current.text))`.
- `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatInput.tsx`:
  - `historyDirection(key: Key): "previous" | "next" | undefined` returns `"previous"` for an unshifted up arrow.
  - In the `useInput` handler, `ownsNavigation(key) && yieldsNavigation()` returns early when the slash menu owns the key, before escape handling and before `historyDirection`.
  - `atEnd(text: string): EditorState` is an editor holding `text` with the cursor at its end.
  - `publish(next)` writes the draft (editor plus history).

Symbols this feature changes. The baseline only locates the code; implement the target.

- `ChatInputProps` (`ChatInput.tsx`)
  - Baseline: has optional `onQueue?: (text: string) => boolean` and `busyNow?: () => boolean`; no recall callback.
  - Target: gains optional `onRecallQueued?: () => string | undefined`. The input calls it when a key yields `historyDirection(key) === "previous"`, the slash menu does not own the key, and the current editor text is exactly `""`. A returned string is written into the prompt with `atEnd(text)` (history unchanged, history browsing not started) and the key is consumed. A returned `undefined`, or no callback, falls through to today's history browsing. The owner must not throw.
- `ChatApp` (`ChatApp.tsx`)
  - Baseline: passes `onQueue={queueReturn}` and no recall callback.
  - Target: passes `onRecallQueued={recallQueued}`, where `recallQueued()` reads `queueRef.current`; for an empty queue it returns `undefined`; otherwise it calls `replaceQueue(EMPTY_QUEUE)` and returns `queueToPrompt(queue, "")`.
- `HINT_PARTS.queued` (`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/chat-status.ts`)
  - Baseline: `{ gesture: "esc to interrupt", extra: "ctrl+s to send queued now" }`.
  - Target: `{ gesture: "esc to interrupt", extra: "up to edit queued · ctrl+s to send now" }`.
- `CHAT_KEYBOARD_HELP` (`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/help-text.ts`)
  - Baseline: ends with `"ctrl+s  steer the running turn (or interrupt and send)"`.
  - Target: the same rows followed by one new last row `"up  edit queued messages (empty prompt)"`.

Approach

Recall all queued messages into the prompt at once (Claude Code's behaviour), reusing `queueToPrompt` and `replaceQueue`. Emptying the queue at the keypress, through `queueRef`, is what keeps a drain from sending a line the user is editing: once recalled, the text is in the prompt and nowhere else. Rejected: recalling only the newest line per press (keeps message boundaries but differs from the behaviour the user expects) and an in-place picker (needs a drain lock for a queue of one to three lines).

Interactions with existing state, all unchanged by this feature:

- A pending interrupt-send (`interruptSend`) is not in the queue and is not recalled.
- Pending steers (the `steering · <text>` rows) are not in the queue and are not recalled.
- The discarded-steer group (`discardedSteers`) needs no reset: `pushDiscardedSteer` already starts a new group when the queue no longer begins with the old one.
- A recalled draft returned while a turn still runs goes through `onQueue` as one queued message; returned once no turn runs, it is submitted as a typed return.

Failure Handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|:---|:---|
| Up with an empty queue and an empty prompt | `recallQueued` returns `undefined`; history browsing runs as today |
| Up with text in the prompt | The callback is not called; history browsing runs as today |
| Up while the slash menu owns the key | The menu keeps the key; the callback is not called |
| Shift+up | Not a history key; the callback is not called and the viewport scrolls as today |
| A drain fires after the recall | The queue is already empty, so nothing is sent and the prompt is untouched |

**Scope** — In: optional input callback, synchronous owner queue recall, queued footer/help wording, and regression tests in existing suites. Out: no inter-story exclusions; this PRD has only US-001. Nearby feature boundaries: Editing, removing or reordering one queued message in place, or a picker over the queue. Recalling a steer the brain already accepted, or the pending interrupt-send, into the prompt. Keeping queued messages as separate messages after recall: a recalled draft is re-queued or sent as one message. Image attachments: a picture travels as a placeholder in the prompt text, so an empty prompt carries none and the recall touches no attachment state. Editing `.nax/features/chat-steer-and-polish/spec.md`: it is a historical record of a shipped feature.

**Interface** — Spec signatures:
```typescript
onRecallQueued?: () => string | undefined
type MessageQueue = readonly string[]
queueToPrompt(queue: MessageQueue, draft: string): string
replaceQueue(next: MessageQueue): void
queueReturn(text: string): boolean
historyDirection(key: Key): "previous" | "next" | undefined
atEnd(text: string): EditorState
```

Implementation/test notes: extend existing ChatInput component harnesses and the chat-steer-queued screen harness; assert all framed prompt rows for multiline recall, the cursor-at-end state, callback counts, history fallback and key ownership. Explicitly settle completed and cancelled turns after recall, and observe host.send rather than queue internals. Update chat-status-queued.test.ts's exact extra expectation and chat-steer-queued.test.tsx's QUEUED_GESTURE to `up to edit queued · ctrl+s to send now`, retaining its footer-row assertion at the helper's default terminal width. Append the literal help row to TARGET_KEYBOARD_HELP in help-text.test.ts, change existing nine-row count expectations to ten and rename the two nine-row test titles. No new queue helpers, drain locks or files are required.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] In the chat screen with a turn running, after `first` and `second` are queued with return, pressing up on the empty prompt makes the prompt hold `first\nsecond`: two prompt rows, `first` above `second` (the test reads every prompt row, not only the last `>` row).
[integration] In the same state, after pressing up, the screen draws no `queued ·` row.

[integration] After recalling `first` and `second` with up while the turn still runs, pressing return draws exactly one `queued ·` row, and when the turn ends `completed` the host's `send` receives the text `first\nsecond` as one message.
[integration] After recalling `first` with up while the turn runs, when the running turn ends `completed` the host's `send` is not called with `first` until the user presses return.
[integration] After recalling `first` with up while the turn runs, when the running turn ends `cancelled` the prompt still holds exactly `first`, not `first` twice.
[integration] With a turn running, `first` queued and `draft` typed in the prompt, pressing up does not put `first` into the prompt and the `queued · first` row stays drawn.
[integration] With nothing queued, an empty prompt and `earlier` in the input history, pressing up puts `earlier` in the prompt, as before this feature.
[integration] With a turn running and `first` queued, pressing shift+up leaves the prompt empty and the `queued · first` row drawn.
[unit] `ChatInput` rendered with an `onRecallQueued` callback returning `recalled`, given an up arrow on an empty prompt, shows `recalled` with the cursor at its end and calls the callback once.
[unit] `ChatInput` rendered with an `onRecallQueued` callback returning `undefined` and `earlier` in its history, given an up arrow on an empty prompt, shows `earlier`.
[unit] `ChatInput` rendered with an `onRecallQueued` callback and the text `abc` in the prompt, given an up arrow, does not call the callback.
[unit] `hintSpans("queued")` returns the gesture `esc to interrupt` and the extra `up to edit queued · ctrl+s to send now`.
[unit] The last row of `CHAT_KEYBOARD_HELP` is `up  edit queued messages (empty prompt)`.
[unit] Given an empty prompt, an onRecallQueued callback and yieldNavigation returning true, when up is pressed, ChatInput does not call onRecallQueued because the open slash menu owns the key.

[integration] Given an open slash menu with at least two matches and the second match selected, when up is pressed while the menu owns navigation, the first match becomes selected, preserving existing menu navigation.
[unit] Given an empty prompt and an onRecallQueued callback, when shift+up is pressed, ChatInput does not call onRecallQueued.

[integration] Given queued messages and a transcript with at least one scrollable row above the visible window, when shift+up is pressed, the viewport moves one line toward older transcript content, as today.

[integration] Given `first` recalled into the prompt, no new queued messages and no pending interrupt-send, when the running turn settles as completed or cancelled, the prompt still holds exactly `first` after the drain.

[integration] Given a recalled draft, no new queued messages and no pending interrupt-send, when the running turn settles as completed or cancelled, host.send's call count remains unchanged after the drain.

[unit] Given text `abc` in the first editor row, history [`earlier`], no active history browse and an onRecallQueued callback, when up is pressed, ChatInput shows `earlier` through existing history browsing.

routing.reasoning: Four focused source edits reuse existing owner callbacks, synchronous queue refs, editor publishing and queue-to-prompt formatting; no new abstraction, dependency, cross-package API or security-critical path is introduced. TDD should exercise drain races and navigation regressions through the existing component and screen harnesses.

suggestedCriteria: Given an onRecallQueued callback and a prompt containing exactly three spaces, when up is pressed, the callback is not called.
Given an empty prompt and history containing earlier, when onRecallQueued returns recalled on up, the published draft retains the same history and has no browse position.
Given an empty prompt, history containing earlier and an onRecallQueued callback returning an empty string, when up is pressed, the prompt stays empty rather than displaying earlier.
Given first queued during a running turn, when up and then a printable x arrive before a re-render, the prompt becomes firstx and no queued row remains.

modifiedFiles.reason: "AC-13 names the interrupt as its gesture and ctrl+s as its extra" asserts the queued hint's extra is `ctrl+s to send queued now`; it becomes `up to edit queued · ctrl+s to send now`, gesture unchanged.

`QUEUED_GESTURE` pins `ctrl+s to send queued now` for "AC-14 offers ctrl+s to send queued now on the footer row"; it becomes `up to edit queued · ctrl+s to send now`, and the test still asserts the footer row shows it while a line is queued at the helper's default terminal width (the title may be renamed to match).

`TARGET_KEYBOARD_HELP` pins the exact keyboard help rows; it gains the new last row `up  edit queued messages (empty prompt)` after the ctrl+s row, and the count assertions in "AC-1 is the nine-line block the spec fixes, joined with newlines" and "names the nine rows the block has, Keyboard first" (`toHaveLength(9)`) become ten rows; the test titles say ten.

analysis:
Refine audit: re-read the on-disk feature spec and current input, drain, queue, menu and test code. Spec acceptance criteria are preserved in US-001 in their original order: (1) oldest-first multiline prompt, including the every-prompt-row parenthetical; (2) no queued row after recall; (3) one requeued message and one multiline host send on completed; (4) no automatic send before return after completed; (5) no duplicate draft after cancelled; (6) typed-draft exclusion with queue row retained; (7) empty-queue history fallback, retaining as before this feature; (8) shift+up exclusion; (9) callback once and cursor at end; (10) undefined callback result falls through to history; (11) nonempty prompt does not call the callback; (12) exact queued hint gesture and extra; (13) exact final help row. All five failure-table rows are covered by these and the explicit menu, shifted-navigation, drain and nonempty-history criteria. Tightened vague menu/viewport assertions into observable selection and one-line viewport changes and specified no pending interrupt-send for drain-only expectations. These anchors match packages/nax/src/tui/chat/SlashMenu.tsx:177-183 (clamped pointer movement), :204 (up moves -1), and packages/nax/src/tui/chat/TranscriptViewport.tsx:85-93 (shift+up maps to lineUp). No description/AC contradictions were found. All seven feature exclusions remain verbatim at top level; adjacent exclusions remain echoed in the story scope. The five contextFiles exactly match the spec's Context Files list. The binding single US-001, packages/nax workdir and empty dependencies are unchanged. Medium/tdd-simple remains appropriate for four focused source edits; regression anchors cover existing history, menu and viewport behavior. No new files or dependencies are necessary.

This is an enhancement to the existing React/Ink chat TUI, entirely within packages/nax. Codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this host, so discovery used direct reads and text search. No implementation or test commands were run while drafting or refining this PRD.

Architecture and existing behavior: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/message-queue.ts:28 defines MessageQueue as readonly string[], oldest first; :119 implements queueToPrompt(queue, draft) by filtering only empty strings and joining with newlines. Reuse it unchanged; do not trim message contents or invent a second join algorithm. pushDiscardedSteer at :94 already recognizes a discarded group only while the queue starts with its texts; an explicit reset on recall is unnecessary. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx:348 keeps the authoritative queueRef ahead of React, and :384 replaceQueue synchronously writes queueRef.current and setQueued together. queueReturn at :875 appends through that helper and rejects drafts carrying images. drainQueue at :1097 prioritizes interruptSend, then reads queueRef.current at :1108 and immediately returns on an empty queue at :1109; a non-completed outcome clears and restores the queue at :1111-1112, whereas completed outcomes remove and submit one queued message. Recall must empty queueRef synchronously, not merely schedule setQueued, so a later drain cannot send or duplicate the recalled draft. Do not change interruptSend precedence or pending-steer handling. The ChatInput binding at :1422-1443 currently supplies onQueue={queueReturn}, busyNow={() => sending.current}, and yieldNavigation={mention.ownsNavigation}; add the owner callback alongside these props. changeDraft at :1256 updates editorRef at :1259, so recalled text should travel through ChatInput's publish/onDraftChange path rather than an out-of-band owner editor update.

Input integration: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatInput.tsx:82 declares ChatInputProps, with onQueue at :135 and busyNow at :144. Add optional onRecallQueued?: () => string | undefined and document its non-throwing owner contract. historyDirection at :546 excludes shifted arrows; atEnd at :564 computes cursor length with Array.from(text), preserving Unicode code-point cursor semantics. The useInput handler at :772 yields navigation to the open menu before escape/history handling and reads latest.current, not a stale draft prop. Intercept only direction === previous and current.editor.text === empty string before previousEntry; do not substitute trim(), reuse the ctrl+s empty-draft rule, or add an unnecessary busy guard. A defined returned string, including an empty string, consumes the key, publishes editor: atEnd(text), preserves history, and leaves browsing unset; undefined or an omitted callback keeps the existing history path. publish at :649 writes the local latest ref before notifying the owner, so batched keys retain earlier edits. submit at :709 already queues the full multiline draft as one message when running and submits it after a turn becomes idle, using busyNow to avoid render races. No new submit path is needed.

Source changes: ChatInput.tsx, ChatApp.tsx, packages/nax/src/tui/chat/chat-status.ts:203 (HINT_PARTS.queued), and packages/nax/src/tui/chat/help-text.ts:2-12 (CHAT_KEYBOARD_HELP). message-queue.ts is a read-only dependency. HINT_PARTS.queued must keep gesture esc to interrupt and change extra to up to edit queued · ctrl+s to send now. Append up  edit queued messages (empty prompt) after the ctrl+s help row. Dependents include AskCard.tsx:35 and :641 (another ChatInput caller which must retain default history behavior), bottom-region.ts:18 and frame-surfaces.ts:34 (input measurement), use-image-attach.ts:33 and use-mention-menu.ts:31 (input-handle consumers); none needs a new required prop. slash-commands.ts:20 consumes CHAT_KEYBOARD_HELP, so both native and ACP help inherit the new row. footer-segments.ts:59-61 consumes hintSpans and tags the extra as gestureExtra, which the existing fitter can drop. status-layout.ts:1 and ChatApp.tsx:40 consume chat-status. Avoid changing footer fitting policy merely because the new extra is longer.

Tests and implementation sequence: write failing recall behavior tests first, implement the input/owner callback, then update exact hint/help expectations as part of the same US-001. packages/nax/test/ui/chat/chat-steer-queued.test.tsx:18 reuses mountChatPicker from @test/helpers; :69-97 exposes screen verbs, rows, footerRow, explicit turn_end status and send-finally flushing. Reuse this controlled host to test recall, absence of queue rows, requeue-as-one-message, completed/cancelled drains, existing history, typed-draft exclusion and shift+up. Read every prompt row inside the framed input, including continuation rows, instead of just the row beginning with >. The same file's QUEUED_GESTURE at :30 and footer assertion at :171 must change to the exact new extra, retaining the assertion at the helper's default terminal width. packages/nax/test/ui/chat/message-queue.test.tsx:70-115 has a controlled ChatInput owner with observable drafts, and :117 onward tests onQueue. packages/nax/test/ui/chat/chat-input.test.tsx:240 covers history, :410 cursor position, :475 batching and :555 key ownership; extend suitable existing helpers to expose the optional recall callback, initial history, cursor and published draft without replacing internal source functions. The spec labels isolated ChatInput render cases unit tests; repository placement for these component tests is test/ui/chat. Existing queue join tests are packages/nax/test/unit/tui/chat/message-queue.test.ts:44-58. Update packages/nax/test/unit/tui/chat/chat-status-queued.test.ts:58-61 to the exact new extra while retaining the gesture assertion. Update packages/nax/test/unit/tui/chat/help-text.test.ts:17-37 by appending the new literal target row, changing the row count from nine to ten, and renaming both nine-row titles to ten. In this checkout only the second test actually has toHaveLength(9); update every existing nine-row/count expectation rather than introducing a spurious second count requirement. slash-commands-acp.test.ts:156 and :184-187 and slash-memory.test.ts:232 compose expectations from the exported help constant and should inherit the added row. All changes can extend existing source/test files; no new files are required. Use targeted bun test paths with a timeout from packages/nax, never bare bun test; normal lint/typecheck/test are pipeline gates, not acceptance criteria. Follow docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md and package testing rules; do not run coverage inside a sandboxed nax session.

Risk and compatibility: the main risks are a React-state-only clear leaving drainQueue a stale message, publishing recalled text without updating the input's latest ref, accidentally starting history browsing, accepting whitespace as an empty prompt, stealing slash-menu or shifted navigation, losing the first row of a multiline prompt assertion, and duplicating text through cancelled-turn restoration. Keeping the callback optional preserves other ChatInput callers. This is transient UI state, not a session/security-contract change: there is no provider, API, permission, dependency, schema or persistence migration. Recalled messages intentionally lose queue boundaries and become one ordinary multiline draft. Pending interrupt-send and steering rows are not recalled; attachments and historical feature specs remain unchanged. Medium complexity and tdd-simple fit four small source edits using existing owner-callback and queue helpers with no new abstraction or cross-package integration.
outOfScope: Editing, removing or reordering one queued message in place, or a picker over the queue.
Recalling a steer the brain already accepted, or the pending interrupt-send, into the prompt.
Keeping queued messages as separate messages after recall: a recalled draft is re-queued or sent as one message.
Message queues in any front end other than the `nax chat` TUI; the queue does not exist outside `packages/nax/src/tui/chat`.
Persisting the queue across a restart or a session switch.
Image attachments: a picture travels as a placeholder in the prompt text, so an empty prompt carries none and the recall touches no attachment state.
Editing `.nax/features/chat-steer-and-polish/spec.md`: it is a historical record of a shipped feature.
